newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 16.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on May 16. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Indonesia President Suharto has said the country's economy is on the right track despite a number of disturbances during the campaign for the May 29 general elections.
Campaign violence continued across Java on Thursday with sporadic clashes between supporters of the ruling Golkar and their United Development Party (PPP) rivals.

State-owned oil and gas company Pertamina has signed eight production-sharing contracts and four technical assistance contracts for oil and gas exploration with local and foreign companies. The contractors are committed to spending $634.3 million on exploration and production.

Beleaguered Canadian mining company Bre-X Minerals Ltd has earmarked at least $600,000 to pay some 488 employees it plans to lay off following the decision by the Indonesian mines and energy ministry to freeze all its operations in Indonesia. The government froze all Bre-X operations in Indonesia following the announcement of an independent geological survey that there was no gold worth mining at the Busang field in East Kalimantan.
